chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Trombonist Fred Robinson and a possible Willie Gant record
summary: Fred Robinson, who had recorded with Jelly in Chicago, worked on the subway and retired to Cleveland; a Chilton listing of a Gant record puzzles them.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah, I see. Now, the next session, that's right, you have Fred Robinson in place of Claude (unintelligible) and Bechet's out.
That's where you did West End Blues and (unintelligible).
That's right. He was a good trombone player too, Freddy, very good trombone player. Yes, he was.
As a soloist or as an ensemble man?
Well, he was a good all around man.

Uh-huh, he's living back in Cleveland now. I got his address too. I don't know whether he's records or not I'll get an answer from him, probably mail him one. He had made records with Jelly before with the Red Hot Peppers in Chicago. Then when he came to New York, he was working on the subway. I don't know whether he was -- I think he was a conductor. Yeah, I think he must have retired because Fred went back to Cleveland.
Well, he must be getting on by now, anyway.
Oh, definitely, he got to be.
(Unintelligible). Well then, so then we come, according to Chilton, he's got this record with Willie Gant. I don't know anything about that. I never heard of it.
Let me see now. Did we -- that might have been taped, Stanley, while we were in Small's, Could have been taken off unexpectedly.
Yeah, but Small's was before. I mean they hadn't got tape then.
No, they had no tapes then. You had to go down to the studio those days.
